responseText: {"title":"Figures in Company","question":"When do separate figures begin to form a group?","introduction":"Twenty-three works line this gallery, each placing two or more figures in the same space. The question is not whether they belong together but how the visible evidence — gap, overlap, shared mark, mirrored posture — tips a collection of bodies toward something that reads as a group. Follow the progression and decide for yourself where that threshold falls.","closing":"The works offer no single answer: proximity, shared marks, and overlapping outlines each make a different claim. The threshold between separate and together remains open.","chapters":[{"title":"Two in a Field","introduction":"Six works open the exhibition with pairs held apart by open ground. yellow zigzags scatter between them, filling the gap with static rather than connection.","transitionFromPrevious":"The heart shape of the previous work gave contact a clear sign; here the space between figures is filled with marks that suggest charge without resolving into gesture."},{"slot":"W095","whyHere":"Two gaunt jointed figures share an unbroken orange field; one raises an object toward its own head, the other crouches low — parallel actions that do not address each other.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works use a flat single-color ground with no depth, so the figures' relationship depends entirely on posture and proximity rather than setting."},{"slot":"W175","whyHere":"One expansive open-mouthed figure faces a compact scowling bird-like figure across an open middle ground — the most explicit face-to-face standoff so far.","transitionFromPrevious":"The orange-field pair acted in parallel without facing each other; here the two figures are oriented directly toward one another, making the gap between them feel confrontational."}]},{"title":"Marks Held in Common","introduction":"Five works explore a different kind of togetherness: figures that share repeated visual marks — crossed eyes, spiked crowns, coiled lines — as if the marks themselves are what binds them.","stops":[{"slot":"W283","whyHere":"Two figures carry nearly identical red-circled cross-marked heads against a yellow field; the doubling reads as a bond written directly onto the face.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous chapter's pairs were linked by posture and proximity; here the connection is inscribed in matching marks on each figure's head."},{"slot":"W100","whyHere":"Two large black figures share crossed X-eyes, ringed circles, and tooth rows; this one surrounds both figures with a common visual field, so mark and setting together form the bond."},{"slot":"W251","whyHere":"Two crowned figures with matching red eyes and splayed hands lean toward each other;
